title: Realization of compact-support path equations through the completed limit
statement:
Fix $R=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$, $P_n=R/I^n$ and the finite-field, pro-etale and completed coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. All schemes and maps lie in the compact-support domains of [fix-lem-exchanges]; in particular the schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, all open compactification factors are quasi-compact, and the integral input $K$ and all intermediate objects are derived complete with the compatible finite etale-origin witnesses and amplitude bounds of those domains. On each scheme $T$ put $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline R_T))$ and $L_T=R\lim$ on its derived category [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. Let $\operatorname{Res}_T$ be restriction from completed to constant coefficients, and $\mathcal R_T$ the strict reduction functor, with the completion-unit and finite-reduction normalizations of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].
Let $W$ be a finite well-typed word in completed pullbacks, proper derived direct images and quasi-compact open extensions, with compact support represented by its supplied proper/open factorization [def-exchange-projection, def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]. Let $\widetilde W$ replace these letters by their normalized constant-$R$ strict-tower operations. The specified corner comparison
$$a_{W,K}:\operatorname{Res}(WK)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_T(\widetilde W\operatorname{Res}\mathcal R(K))$$
is obtained recursively from the completion units, the canonical proper direct-image/limit comparison [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], and the open-extension/strict-reduction-limit comparison [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], with the pullback comparisons fixed in the completed exchange definition.
For any composable path $\alpha:W\to V$ whose arrows are the specified compact-support exchanges, pullback compositors or compactification-refinement comparisons on these domains, let $\widetilde\alpha:\widetilde W\to\widetilde V$ be the corresponding constant-tower path, with each proper strict factor the one in [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map] and each open factor the canonical strict open comparison. Then these specified comparisons satisfy
$$a_{V,K}\circ\operatorname{Res}(\alpha_K)=L_T(\widetilde\alpha_{\operatorname{Res}\mathcal R(K)})\circ a_{W,K}.$$
The equation also holds for whiskering such paths by the displayed operation words. In particular, if two such parallel strict paths are equal as derived strict-tower maps, their completed paths are equal. The same conclusion applies to the refinement exchange equations and cocycles. This is a comparison of actual maps using the prescribed source and target identifications; equality of finite evaluated maps is not a hypothesis sufficient for it.

proof.text: Extract endpoint finiteTorConstructibleIntegral from IntegralDomain by cases on each expression (the proved private integralDomain_output helper). Apply completeIntegralConstantRestriction to these two output objects. Their actual scalar completion units are invertible, and each reductionComparison is an isomorphism. Functoriality of total limit therefore makes both prescribed corners invertible.

Apply compactSupportPathReductionSquare to the given prescribed path. The proved private categorical limit_square lemma expands each corner as eta followed by L(q), uses naturality of eta to move H(a) across it, combines the two consecutive L-maps, substitutes the reduction square, and uses map_comp and associativity. Specialize it to constantReduction, constantLimit and the actual completion unit. This proves the displayed square for every Path.

For two parallel paths with equal towerMap, their displayed squares give equal composites H(a) followed by the target corner. Cancel this invertible corner and apply injectivity of H.map between the two complete endpoint objects supplied by completeIntegralConstantRestriction. This gives a=a′ without testing finite evaluations.
